answer.generated: The computational complexity of computing distances using a KD-tree is O(N log N), which is significantly more efficient than the brute-force method of computing distances between all pairs of points, whose complexity is O(N^2). This improvement is particularly beneficial in high-dimensional spaces, where the brute-force approach becomes prohibitively expensive due to the curse of dimensionality. KD-trees offer a practical solution by reducing the number of distance computations needed, thereby optimizing the overall efficiency of the algorithm.
